steps.content: A few minutes ago.
Parfait and the others take Sibilla with them to another hidden location in the slums.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Anyway, I'm just doing a little favor for this new friend of mine. Helping her helps me too.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Sibilla got hurt, and she's really shaken. Can you look after her and keep her out of sight for a bit? Aunt Gracelyn, Mr. Harry, I'm counting on you two.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Well, I'm off! Save the lectures for next time! See you!
She leaves with a smile plastered across her face—or rather, flees the scene—and then...
[White Out, Scene End] (Change to a dilapidated house background)

BANG! A baseball bat is smashed against the floor. The lead woman slams her boot onto the table, looming over Sibilla, who crumples to her knees. She trembles under the woman's intent stare—a clear act of intimidation.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Hey, listen up. I'll make this crystal clear: nobody else alive on this planet knows Parfait's secret except us.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: This is Syndicate. Faking cash is barely worth mentioning. Parfait just whipped up some chump change a few years back—peanuts compared to what the Nirvana suits have taken into their pockets.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Oh, and just so you know, reporting her to that whatever Sinner Bureau won't help you one bit. Their boss is tight with us Syndicans, like thick as thieves.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Parfait's secret's stayed buried 'cause I've been the one cleaning up her messes. If anything leaks from you... well, let's just say I'm very good at taking out the trash. Got it? Answer me!
How can Sibilla possibly speak? Her breath catches in fear, her body trembling—then, a sudden tap. A hand lands on the red-haired woman's shoulder.

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: C'mon, Gracelyn. She's an Outlander—she can barely speak our language. Doubt she even gets what you're saying. Why waste your breath trying to scare her?

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: Why don't you grab some water? You've been ranting forever. Your throat's gotta be parched.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Ugh, why didn't you tell me sooner?? Look at me, all stressed out for nothing! With all that chaos tonight, I totally thought Parfait got into some trouble again and someone was after her.
The red-haired woman visibly relaxes, her entire demeanor softening as she mutters her way into the kitchen. Something about the scene feels strangely familiar to Sibilla.
Meanwhile, the young DisCity man named Harry turns to her, speaking slowly with exaggerated hand gestures. He seems to genuinely believe that Sibilla isn't proficient in Disian.

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: Don't take offense. Gracelyn's just a bit of a worrywart. But hey, if Parfait trusts you with her secret, then we will too. Just don't let anything slip, okay?
Sibilla believes him. After all, if they meant to kill her, she wouldn't still be breathing.

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: Kick back and relax while you're in Syndicate. The Drifter Camp used to have lots of Outlanders around. Later we'll have Greta, our yooga master here, check out your injuries. Trust me, you'll be back on your feet in no time.

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: Oh, by the way, where are you from? Did you come for the Great Expo too? Is that how you met Parfait, through business?

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Thank you, but I'm just a stowaway hiding here, afraid of getting caught. I'm grateful to Parfait for protecting me, and to all of you as well.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Don't worry about me. I'll just wait for her here.
Sibilla's command of Disian is better than Harry's expectations. He smiles awkwardly.

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: Ahaha... You were totally freaked out just now, huh? Don't worry—I got you. Let me fix you up first.

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: But our first aid supplies are pretty basic right now. The West District's still getting set up, so we're a little low on resources.
Harry finishes bandaging her wounds with quick, practiced motions, then releases her and steps back, giving her space.
Sibilla once again crouches silently in the corner, listening attentively.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: I ******* told her to get her ass back already and quit loitering around Eastside! What's the damn point of guarding that chump change? She's got it but won't spend it, won't even open her mouth—just sitting there scared out of her mind every day. For what?!

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: For that if something happens to you, at least she can bail you out as the big-shot stock market guru. But otherwise? Just for that stunt you pulled protesting at the mine, Nirvana would've locked you up until you died.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: I-I was there to expose their damn conspiracy! You think their fancy Great Expo and stock market tricks are legit? Their plot to grab the mine is right in my face! How the hell can Parfait even stand dealing with those snakes? Doesn't it make her sick?!

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: You really think so? I've always thought Parfait's playing the long game. I mean, let's be real—money runs DisCity now, no matter how you slice it. Gotta know your enemy if you wanna come out on top.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Hold up... those guys chasing us earlier... were they after Parfait or that woman? And wait, isn't Nirvana cutting some shady deal with the Fraser people to steal our mine?!

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: No way, did we actually find an ally? Did Sibilla dig up some big secret or what? Parfait's bending over backward to keep her safe, so we better—

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: Yeah, yeah, Gracelyn, by all means—talk a little louder. It's not like those guys outside will hear us and bust in to murder us all or anything.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: !! You little brat...

The red-haired woman is left speechless. Despite their bickering, the air stays light—seemingly just another day in the DisCity slums. From the corner, Sibilla watches, the distance between her and the scene widening with every breath.
Until the door opens, and a black-haired woman walks in.
...Huh, who is this...?

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: <size=36>Shh... I'll explain.</size>
The two move aside and whisper something to each other, then quickly return. The woman's gaze has visibly softened.

steps.speaker: Black-Haired Woman
steps.content: So you're Parfait's friend. You look like you've had a rough time... But don't worry, you're safe here. This place will keep you protected.

steps.speaker: Black-Haired Woman
steps.content: Let me make you something to eat. You can rest properly once you've had some food.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...Thank you.
Sibilla's gaze follows the black-haired woman. The pendant hanging from her wrist... is undoubtedly made of Aurum Secretum.
A sudden tug at Sibilla's clothes jerks her back to reality, tearing her from her daze. She glances down—a boy stares up at her, his face smeared with vibrant paint.

steps.speaker: Allen
steps.content: Who are you staring at, ma'am?

steps.speaker: Ashley
steps.content: Are you an Outlander? Did Parfait bring you back here?

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Huh? Yeah... I am.
The two children exchange a smile.

steps.speaker: Ashley
steps.content: Could you help us with something? It's...
Rising onto her toes, she leans close and whispers something into Sibilla's ear...
[Scene Change]
A few minutes later.
Dirty water seeps from the ventilation ducts, plink-plonking into a metal bucket. Sibilla lifts the bulletproof blanket serving as a door curtain, and the aroma of hot food immediately greets her.

steps.speaker: Black-Haired Woman
steps.content: Go ahead and try some. This budget curry is actually a specialty from the Drifter Camp. Just add a little water, and it has a surprisingly nice flavor.
The black-haired woman in a dark apron ladles a spoonful of curry over rice, then passes the plate to her fellow Outlander, a stranger she's never met.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Thank you. I'm Sibilla. May I ask what your name is?

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: You can call me "Sable."
Sibilla nods, taking a small taste of the curry as she searches for the right words to start a conversation. Then, an idea strikes her.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: It's really good. It doesn't taste like something from DisCity. Where did you learn to make it?

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: I don't remember anymore. My body just naturally knows what to do.
She smiles.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: This Drifter Camp curry was originally a family recipe from an Outland physician, but to say it's not from DisCity, I doubt you know DisCity food that well.
Sibilla's attempt at small talk lands like a stone. Awkwardly, she scratches her head.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: Did the kids send you?

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...Yeah.
[Enter Flashback]

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Why it has to be me...?

steps.speaker: Ashley
steps.content: Because Parfait brought back both of you!

steps.speaker: Ashley
steps.content: When Sable was brought here, she also had wounds all over. We keep asking Parfait about her, but she won't tell us anything! We don't know where Sable's from, or how long she'll stay, or if she has any family or friends. She's being so sneaky about it!

steps.speaker: Allen
steps.content: But I just had a great idea! Since you were both brought back by Parfait all injured, maybe Sable is also an Outlander like you? Maybe you two will have more to talk about!

steps.speaker: Ashley
steps.content: I was just... thinking... what if she leaves DisCity and goes home someday? Not that she shouldn't go home! It's just... um... I'd miss her a lot.

steps.speaker: Allen
steps.content: We haven't talked to her about this yet! A-anyway... can you ask her first? Pleeease? You'll help, right?
Sibilla meets the children's gazes—hope and anxiety shimmering in their eyes—and finally nods. No matter where she is, she can never say no to children.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...Alright, I'll help you.
[Exit Flashback]
After hearing her words, "Sable" breaks into a smile.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: Heh, they're probably worried that if I leave, no one will cook for them anymore.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: Syndicate is slowly rebuilding now, and with many parents working outside the home, those children have been left in my care. I'm happy to help—it's my way of thanking everyone for taking me in so kindly.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: They really don't need to worry. I'm not going anywhere.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: I can't even remember things from three months ago anymore.
Sibilla is stunned at those words.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: Parfait says it's nothing serious, and she's helping me find a doctor to look into it. I'm very grateful to her. Being with the children... it puts me at ease. They always make me feel like I'm so close to remembering something—like that happiness about something important is just out of reach.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: ...But every night, after having the same dream, everything slips away from me again.
Sable turns off the stove and casts her eyes downward.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: In my dreams, I'm always walking in the rain. Through the downpour, I can almost see something, hear someone calling. I want to chase after it, to grasp it. It could be my homeland, my name, my love, my purpose, or just... something I simply cannot let go.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: ...But in the dream, the heavy rain washes it all away—dissolves it until there's nothing left. It's like the burden I've carried for over a decade, the weight etched into my bones... it's just gone. Ripped from me without warning. And all I can do is stand there, watching it disappear through the curtain of rain.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: By the time I wake up, the rain has stopped. Sunlight's coming through, but I can't remember anything anymore.
Sibilla's lips part, but no words come. Her eyes are fixated on the chain bracelet on "Sable's" wrist.
—Aurum Secretum. It's the excessive resonance of Aurum Secretum. She's one of Fraser's people, and worse—she's someone Fraser bled dry, left hollow. How can she even speak these words aloud?

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: ...DisCity may not be my homeland, but I don't have anywhere else to go back to...

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Don't have anywhere else to go back to...

The woman's words thud in Sibilla's chest, stirring a dull, resonant echo. For the first time, the urge to speak swells in her throat, but before she can, a ragged sob cuts through the silence behind her.

steps.speaker: Ashley
steps.content: Sob... Sable, don't be sad. We'll stay with you. We'll help you remember and take you home...

steps.speaker: Allen
steps.content: Even if you do go back, don't forget about us. Come back to visit us when you have time. We'll miss you...
Sable panics, rushing forward to pull the two children into her arms. Their faces are streaked with tears while they've been eavesdropping.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: Oh my, this is... I'm not going anywhere. I'm staying right here.

steps.speaker: Sable
steps.content: With all of you here, I already have a new home. Shhh, it's okay. Don't cry...
She is surely unaware of her own expression. Animated, warm, alive. This is not the face of one who has lost their homeland. Given time, her soul will find solace here.
As if to add fuel to the fire, the door curtain is suddenly thrown open.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Geez, what in the world? Why is everyone crying??

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Hey, Outland lady, why are your eyes all red too? What's up with that?

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: ...PARFAIT, why the **** are you here?!!!
She drags Parfait through the window, and the room erupts into chaos.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Hmgh... please, be gentle! Let's not ruin this touching moment with violence. That actually hurts—

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: The hell are you doing?! Didn't I just tell you to go back to the other side?! Sneaking in and outta the slums at a time like this... What if someone catches you?!!!

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Ahem, elegant, be elegant! I've already checked outside. Everything's fine. No pursuers, no prying reporters, not a single suspicious soul in sight. Just let me relax a bit.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Since everyone's feeling a bit gloomy, let's brighten the mood! Try this popular mood-lifting remedy from Eastside—the big streamer Thalia's go-to recommendation and my personal taste test approval: a premium blend cooler!
She pulls out a glass bottle with a uniquely shaped body. Just then, footsteps sound behind her as someone walks into the room.

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: Shh... keep it down! That gimmicky fancy drink is a no-go with Gracelyn. The fancier it is, the more she can't stand it. Nothing grinds her gears like rich people acting all high and mighty.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Don't worry.

Parfait hurls sparkling juice and ice into a jug, cuts a lemon in half, and squeezes it with a deft twist of her wrist. A splash of ginger juice follows. She shakes it well, then pours the drink in one smooth motion, raising the glass high like a trophy.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Ta-da! Presenting Parfait's budget special blend, crafted for under fifty DisCoins a glass, but delivering every bit of the joy. It's the magic of a gentle buzz, a moment that belongs only to you.

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: HUH?! It's not the damn money I hate—it's your punch-worthy act! Flaunting, wasting, showing off like some high-and-mighty snob! I'm not going to touch it. Never—OWWW!

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Even if it's just ginger juice mixed with fruit sugar, one should approach it with unhurried enjoyment and a mindset that savors life.
Gracelyn opens her mouth to argue, but the children—their tears already forgotten—bounce past her, teeming with excitement.

steps.speaker: Ashley & Allen
steps.content: Yay!! Yummy drinks!!
[Everyone's stuffed and sprawled out.]

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Tch, all this just to jack those rich pricks' bougie-ass style. The hell's so special about some slinging ginger juice in some overpriced bottle?! Hic! This ain't even a damn drink—what, Eastsiders actually—hic!—guzzle this stuff? Ugh... my stomach's so gassy...

steps.speaker: Gracelyn
steps.content: Huff... Stop hanging out with those guys. Come back to Syndicate...

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: You say you don't want it, but you can't stop drinking. Let's be real, you love this stuff.

steps.speaker: Harry
steps.content: Sorry we can't treat you to something nicer, Sibilla. We're just making do with cheap stuff for now, but just wait. Next time you visit, this place is gonna blow your mind!
The little girl also crawls over.

steps.speaker: Ashley
steps.content: This fruit candy is super cheap... I got it from trading with the Homeless. Will you think it's yucky, Sibilla...

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...Of course I won't. Thank you for your gift.
The girl flashes a bright grin, then pulls out another candy and presses it into Sibilla's palm.

steps.speaker: Ashley
steps.content: Here's another one for you! Thank you for talking so nice with Sable!

As hard candies are dropped into the ginger juice, a dozen hands around the tin table suddenly raise their glasses in unison. The thunderous cheers that follow send a resonant hum trembling through the rusty roof.
Sibilla imitates the others, pressing her fruit candy to the bottom of her glass. Sparkling bubbles swarm around it, sending the little candy dancing up and down in the fizz.
Until someone grabs her hand and pulls it upward.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Come on, it's all about the ritual. Cheers—

steps.speaker: Everyone
steps.content: Cheers!

As laughter and banter swirl around her, Sibilla feels a hazy sense of déjà vu, as if such joy belonged to another life. The weight of a glass in her hand is familiar; the chorus of laughter is distant yet remembered.
Even that piece of fruit candy brings back a moment long past, a taste unforgettable in her lifetime.
She is grateful for her luck, grateful that kindness still exists in this world, that DisCity and Furor, despite everything, still hold something in common. She should be laughing with them...
But in the end, Sibilla only murmurs a hollow reply before lowering her head.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Ch-cheers...

Morning light finds Sibilla blinking awake. Parfait is already gone, the children sent home, and only Harry's scribbled note remains—he went out to work. Gracelyn lies sprawled out in a messy slumber.
Sunlight pours through the open window, carrying the sharp trill of birdsong. Still half-caught in the remnants of her own dreams, Sibilla reaches for the television, groggily turning it on.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Through our ongoing collaborative efforts, DisCity and Fraser have successfully overcome numerous longstanding barriers between us. We're now pleased to announce an expansion of our partnership across economic development, technological exchange, and security intelligence sharing.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Especially targeting the Outland extremists who have recently emerged to disrupt DisCity's peace.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: They operate under clever disguises—the Great Expo personnel, merchant caravans, and even Outland refugees—all to infiltrate DisCity, using a calculated blend of truth and lies to cultivate sympathy and trust. Yet behind this facade, they've been conspiring with Underground extremists, secretly plotting destruction...
[Horo's Photo Displayed]

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: I'm pleased to report we've fostered mutual trust with the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control. Critical intelligence on Underground infiltration has been shared, and Chief ${PlayerName} has provided invaluable combat experience. This partnership will continue to deepen moving forward.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: As for those dangerous Outland elements hiding within DisCity...

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: We are determined to locate and address every one of them. In the meantime, we kindly request all citizens to come forward with any relevant information. For immediate reporting, please contact...

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: No... that's not true... He's lying!!
Sibilla abruptly stands up, disregarding any threat of pursuit or assassination, and bolts out of the dingy alley in a blind panic.
